hints.title: Initial Login Date Grouping
hints.text: Identify each user first login date, then count how many users had their initial login on each date in the ninety-day window.

hints.title: Earliest Date Subquery with Range Filter
hints.text: Group activity by user for login actions to find minimum dates. Filter dates within ninety days up to 2019-06-30 and count users.

hints.title: Daily New Users Blueprint
hints.text: select login_date, count(user_id) as user_count from (select user_id, min(activity_date) as login_date from Traffic where activity = "login" group by user_id) t where login_date between "2019-04-01" and "2019-06-30" group by login_date.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT login_date, COUNT(user_id) AS user_count
FROM (
    SELECT user_id, MIN(activity_date) AS login_date
    FROM Traffic
    WHERE activity = 'login'
    GROUP BY user_id
) t
WHERE login_date BETWEEN '2019-04-01' AND '2019-06-30'
GROUP BY login_date;
```

variables: T: number of traffic log entries
complexity.notes: Filtering on login activity, aggregating minimum date per user, and grouping by date runs in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Counting raw login events on each day counts returning users instead of strictly first-time new users.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Nested subquery reduces raw events down to one record per distinct user before window aggregation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of MIN(activity_date) per user and DATEDIFF or BETWEEN for the 90-day window.

FROM (
    SELECT user_id, MIN(activity_date) AS login_date
    FROM Traffic

    GROUP BY user_id

WHERE login_date BETWEEN '2019-04-01' AND '2019-06-30'

import pandas as pd

def new_users_daily_count(traffic: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    logins = traffic[traffic['activity'] == 'login']
    first_logins = logins.groupby('user_id')['activity_date'].min().reset_index()
    first_logins.rename(columns={'activity_date': 'login_date'}, inplace=True)
    valid = first_logins[(first_logins['login_date'] >= '2019-04-01') & (first_logins['login_date'] <= '2019-06-30')]
    res = valid.groupby('login_date')['user_id'].count().reset_index()
    return res.rename(columns={'user_id': 'user_count'})
solutions.approach: Pandas Groupby Minimum Login and Window Aggregation
